what: The shape sets this bench is allowed to generate kernels for, and the source of every value in each one.
why_a_registry: A kernel corpus is only as meaningful as the shapes it uses. A plausible-looking middle configuration benchmarks nothing, and once generated it is indistinguishable from a real one. So a shape set may not be generated until its source is recorded here, and a generator refuses an entry whose status is not `sourced`.

statuses.sourced: Every value is read from the named source. Generation is allowed.
statuses.awaiting_source: The model is wanted in this bench, but nobody has supplied the configuration its shapes must come from. Generation is REFUSED. This is a question for a person, not a gap to fill with a guess.

v41.ATTN_S_source: S = 8 is the engine's own attention block size, not a decode-time guess. The engine launches `ds4_attn_sink_batched` over blocks of 8 positions (rust/bench/engine/tile/attn_sink_1head_1blk.tile: 'ONE HEAD, 1 block(s) of 8, D=512'), and the engine's CPU reference pushes `attn_sinks[h]` as an EXTRA score, applies 1/sqrt(head_dim) to every QK score, and starts the weighted-sum loop at scores[1] (rust/ds4-rs-ascend/crates/engine_core/src/attn_dispatch.rs:1428-1490), i.e. the sink is a virtual position with no V. Read 2026-11-10.

kimi_k3.source: the released model's OWN config.json at moonshotai/Kimi-K3 on Hugging Face, read 2026-11-02. Every value below is a key from that file. This is the first of the two candidate sources the earlier note named, and it is the authoritative one -- an adjacent-generation config from a model zoo would give numbers that are not comparable with these.
kimi_k3.source_correction: This entry read `awaiting_source` with the note 'blocked on the file, not only on a decision', on the grounds that no Kimi K3 GGUF is on this machine (the published quant is 94 shards, ~594 GB). That conflated the WEIGHTS with the CONFIGURATION. The shapes live in a 7 KB config.json, and GLM 5.3's came from metadata rather than from tensors too. The block was never the file.
kimi_k3.architecture_note: A 69/24 KDA-to-MLA hybrid over 93 blocks, one of them dense. Two things separate it from GLM 5.3 and both change what the corpus can hold. (1) `hidden_act` is `situ`, not SwiGLU, carrying two beta parameters -- so the dense FFN and the expert FFN are NOT expressible here, where GLM 5.3's were. (2) N_EXP is 896 = 7 x 128, so the expert count DOES admit f32 tiling, where GLM 5.3's 288 admits none. The router is sigmoid + top-k with `noaux_tc`, not softmax + top-k.

glm_5_3.note: `glm5-next` is a hybrid, and the corpus reflects that rather than hiding it: 34 of the 46 blocks use a gated delta net and 12 use MLA, 43 FFNs are a 288-expert MoE and 3 are dense, and there is no RoPE at all (`rope_dimension_count = 0`). The tile API can express the norms, the projections, the dense FFN, the router, the shared expert and the output head. It CANNOT express the delta-net recurrence or its 4-step causal convolution -- those are listed with the intrinsic each would need in gen_glm_5_3.py's UNEXPRESSIBLE table and omitted rather than approximated, because a recurrence written as something else is a different kernel.
glm_5_3.source: the GLM-5.3-Flash-Q2 GGUF's own metadata keys (`glm5-next.*`), read with the engine's metadata dumper on 2026-11-02. Every value below is a key from that file, not a tensor-shape inference and not a choice.
glm_5_3.ATTN_S_source: index_topk = 2048 from zai-org/GLM-5.3 config.json (read 2026-11-10): the DSA indexer selects the top 2048 KV positions and the sparse decode attention attends to those. No attn_sinks key exists in the config, so the sink-free 1-query form is faithful. qk_head_dim/v_head_dim 256 match KEY_LENGTH 256.
